  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Due to the existing COVID - 19 health emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to Assembly Bill 361, please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and address the City Council Meeting of Tuesday, March 22, 2022, at 2:00 p.m. (or 1:00 p.m. if Closed Session) by call- in, video, other electronic means, and from the Gladys Waddingham Lecture Hall, as follows:

1.  Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Comments received after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  March 22, 2022

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
March 22, 2022, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:02 p.m.

The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Finance
Authority Secretary/Parking Authority Secretary/Joint Powers Authority Secretary
announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/
  Finance Authority Chairman/ Parking Authority Chairman/ Joint
  Powers Authority Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor
  Agency Members/Housing Authority Members/ Finance Authority
  Members/ Parking Authority Members/Joint Powers Authority
  Members Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority
  Member/Finance Authority Member/Parking Authority Member/Joint
  Powers Authority Member Dotson.

City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Finance Authority/ Parking Authority/ Joint
Powers officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance Authority,
Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Parking Authority
Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons
present who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing
Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority on any item on
the Agendas, other than the public hearings.

Emily Dixon commented on Agenda Item No. DR-2, Award of a contract and approval of
an agreement with Stephen Doreck Equipment Rentals, Inc., for the Water Main
Replacement FY 2021-22 Project, per Bid No. CB 22-02.

Caller (Name Unknown) spoke concerning a matter not on the Agenda, and was advised
to call back towards the general comment portion of the meeting.

Cedric Morris, Thomas Safran & Associates commented on Agenda Item Nos. DR-5,
Approval of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) regarding the Inglewood Transit
Connector (ITC) Construction Commitments with ST Market D3, LLC, and DR-6,
Approval of a MOU regarding the Market Street Revitalization Efforts with BE-Queen
Market, LLC.

Darrell Goode, Branch President of Santa Monica’s NAACP, commented on PH-1, and
was advised to wait until the public hearing to address his concerns.
   March 22, 2022

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  March 17, 2022, in the amount of $4,032,023.20, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member
  Dotson.

126  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ORDINANCE NO. 22-06 INTRODUCED –
  ADOPTION OF THE FINAL DRAFT MAP AS THE NEW COUNCIL DISTRICT
  BOUNDARIES IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE FAIR MAPS ACT. The City Clerk
  announced the next scheduled matter was a public hearing to receive and file public
  comments on the Proposed Redistricting Maps, and that notice was given in the time,
  form and manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file, and no communications
  were received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented the Staff Report dated March 22, 2022.

  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk gave a brief oral report regarding Map D, which was
  selected by the Mayor and Council Members during the March 15, 2022, public hearing.
  She also stated that the City had 174 days to get Map D adopted, and sent to the County
  Registrar Recorders Office for the November 2022 Election.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  Caller (Name Unknown) question why the fourth map worked best for Inglewood.

  Darrell Goode, Branch President of Santa Monica’s NAACP, disagreed with the
  redistricting process. He stated there were concerns and complaints because the residents
  weren’t properly notified. He also stated the community would like to get involved, and
  he intended to contact someone regarding the redistricting of the City.

  Kelli Clift, spoke concerning a settlement from being a victims of crime at the Regent
  Hotel on La Brea. She stated because of the redistricting process she would like to
  receive a settlement, and housing.

  Mayor Butts closed public comments at the hour of 2:17 p.m.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that further
  reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  Ordinance No. 22-06 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA ADOPTING BOUNDARIES FOR ITS
  COUNCIL DISTRICTS IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE FAIR
  MAPS ACT FOLLOWING THE 2020 FEDERAL CENSUS

  2
   March 22, 2022

  be introduced. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

183  PUBLIC HEARING CONTINUED – CONSIDER AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD 1) ADDING SECTION 2-201 OF ARTICLE 5
  (PURCHASING) OF CHAPTER 2 (ADMINISTRATION); 2) ADDING SECTION
  5-112.1 OF ARTICLE 7 (WATER CONSERVATION) OF CHAPTER 5
  (OFFENSES, MISCELLANEOUS); 3) ADDING SECTION 7-53 OF ARTICLE 5
  (SOLID WASTE CODE) OF CHAPTER 7 (SANITATION AND HEALTH
  REGULATIONS); AND 4) ADDING SECTION 7-79 OF ARTICLE 7
  (CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION RECYCLING PROGRAM) OF
  CHAPTER 7 (SANITATION AND HEALTH REGULATIONS).

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing to be continued to the Council Meeting of April
  5, 2022, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on March 1, 2022, and
  March 8, 2022, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims Pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1) Veronica Aquino for alleged personal injury; dangerous condition on September 22,
  2021.
  2) Maria Gonzalez for personal injury; dangerous condition on August 27, 2021.
  3) Jeremy Wenninger for alleged tire damage; road defect on January 5, 2022.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the City Council does hereby reject claims listed as A-1 through A-3. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

125& 183  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – TELECOM LAW FIRM, PC. Staff report dated
  March 22, 2022, was presented recommending authorization of payment of outstanding
  invoices submitted by Telecom Law Firm, PC, for legal services rendered for assisting in
  the ongoing negotiation of an agreement between the City and MOX Networks, LLC.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the total amount of $9,603.75. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;

  for Building Inspection consulting services.

171  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 21-117 APPROVED - BATEMAN

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 21-117 in an
  annual amount not to exceed $795,600 (total contract amount of $1,591,200). The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

171  AMENDMENT NINE OF THE ELDERLY NUTRITION PROGRAM SERVICES
  SUBAWARD NO. ENP202107 APPROVED – COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES
  WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AGING AND COMMUNITY SERVICES
  (WDACS) RESOLUTION NO. 22-62 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE 2021-2022
  ANNUAL BUDGET. Staff report dated March 22, 2022, was presented recommending
  approval of Amendment Nine of the Elderly Nutrition Program Services Subaward
  Number ENP202107 (City Agreement No. 20-201) with County of Los Angeles
  Workforce Development Aging and Community Services (WDACS) to allocate CDA
  ARP Act funding in the amount of $236,000 for provision of the Elderly Nutrition
  Program (ENP).

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amendment Nine; and 2) Adopt Resolution
  No. 22-62 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD AMENDING THE 2021-2022 ANNUAL BUDGET TO
  RECEIVE $236,000 FROM THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES
  WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AGING AND COMMUNITY
  SERVICES FOR PROVISION OF THE ELDERLY NUTRITION
  PROGRAM (“ENP”)
